ja: 昨日の会議で、もっとはっきり反対しておけばよかった。
en: I wish I had disagreed more clearly at yesterday's meeting.
alternatives: I should have objected more clearly at yesterday's meeting.
I wish I'd pushed back more clearly in yesterday's meeting.
point: 過去の後悔は wish の後に had＋過去分詞

ja: 会議が始まったときには、部長はもう資料を読み終えていました。
en: The manager had already finished reading the materials when the meeting started.
alternatives: When the meeting started, the manager had already read the materials.
By the time the meeting began, the manager had already gone through the materials.
point: 先に終わっていた方は had + 過去分詞

ja: 窓側に座っている女性が、新しいプロジェクトのリーダーです。
en: The woman sitting by the window is the leader of the new project.
alternatives: The woman sitting near the window is the new project leader.
The woman by the window is the leader of the new project.
point: sitting by the window が後ろから woman を説明する

ja: その件は私たちが前回の会議で話し合いましたが、それ以降状況がかなり変わっています。
en: We discussed that issue at the last meeting, but the situation has changed quite a bit since then.
alternatives: We talked about that at our last meeting, but things have changed a lot since then.
We went over that issue in the last meeting, but the situation has changed considerably since then.
point: 前回は過去形、since then 以降は現在完了

ja: この件、もう1時間も話し合っていますよね。そろそろまとめませんか？
en: We've been discussing this for an hour now, so shall we wrap it up?
alternatives: We've been talking about this for an hour. Why don't we wrap it up?
We've been discussing this for an hour, so should we start wrapping up?
point: 1時間ずっと続いていることは have been + -ing

ja: 部長は先週の会議で、この案は来月までに承認されるだろうと言っていましたよ。
en: At last week's meeting, the manager said this proposal would be approved by next month.
alternatives: The manager said at last week's meeting that this proposal would be approved by next month.
At the meeting last week, the manager told us this proposal would get approved by next month.
point: said の後は will を would に下げる

ja: 次の議題に移る前に、予算の数字をもう一度確認できないかと思っていたのですが。
en: I was wondering if we could go over the budget figures once more before we move on.
alternatives: I was wondering whether we could go through the budget numbers again before moving on.
I was hoping we could go over the budget figures one more time before we move on.
point: 過去進行形 was wondering で柔らかい提案に

ja: 私が一番気になっているのは、このプロジェクトの最終的な責任者が誰になるのか、私たちがまだ決めていないことです。
en: What concerns me most is that we still haven't decided who will ultimately be responsible for this project.
alternatives: What worries me most is that we still haven't decided who'll ultimately be responsible for this project.
What bothers me most is that we haven't yet decided who will be ultimately responsible for this project.
point: What 節を主語に、who 以下は平叙文の語順

ja: すべてのフィードバックを検討した結果、チームはリリースを来四半期に延期することに決めました。
en: Having reviewed all the feedback, the team decided to postpone the launch until next quarter.
alternatives: After reviewing all the feedback, the team decided to push the launch back to next quarter.
Having gone through all the feedback, the team decided to delay the launch until next quarter.
point: 先に終えた動作は Having + 過去分詞で表す

ja: 会議が終わるまでに結論が出なかったら、来週またこの話を続けましょう。
en: If we don't reach a decision by the time the meeting ends, let's pick this up again next week.
alternatives: If we haven't reached a decision by the end of the meeting, let's continue this next week.
If we can't come to a conclusion before the meeting ends, let's pick this up again next week.
point: 「終わるまでに」も未来だが節の中は現在形 ends

ja: もし予算がもっとあれば、私たちはこの案に賛成するんですが。
en: If we had a bigger budget, we would support this proposal.
alternatives: If we had more budget, we'd agree to this proposal.
We would support this plan if we had a bigger budget.
point: 現実と違う仮定は if 節を過去形、主節は would

ja: 次の議題に移る前に、この件について何か情報があれば共有してもらえますか？
en: Before we move on to the next item, could you share any information you have on this?
alternatives: Could you share any information you have about this before we move on to the next item?
Before we go on to the next topic, could you share whatever information you have on this?
point: information は数えられないので an や -s をつけない
